text:
Dylan Cozens had the week a second-year Senator wants: two goals in the overtime loss to Philadelphia, including a one-timer from the slot, then two assists against Los Angeles. That makes eight points in his last ten and 16 in 24 games, a fair return for a centre playing 17:27 a night who throws hits like a checking forward (59 of them already).

The finishing is close to normal, six goals on 6.55 expected. What isn't settled is the five-on-five impact. Ottawa takes 51.2% of the expected goals with him on, but nearly five points less than when he sits. That is a change from 2025-26, when Evolving-Hockey rated him 2.0 wins above replacement, 53rd among forwards, with most of it on defense: opponents got 0.22 fewer expected goals per 60 against him, 98th percentile.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking explains how he scores: 53% of his shots came off the rush, so the moments right after a turnover are when the Workhorse from Whitehorse is most dangerous. Our numbers project 56 points and 24 goals, with a range of 47 to 67 points.
headline: Cozens has found his feet in Ottawa
